page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a virtual machine powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It is configured with 4 dedicated virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores utilizing simultaneous multithreading, along with 16 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes a 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, supporting modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 (f, vnni, bf16) and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance features no attached local NVMe storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top 25% for single-threaded stress-ng tests. However, its overall multi-threaded throughput and memory bandwidth metrics show clear hardware trade-offs, falling into the bottom 25% for multi-core stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and uncached large-block memory read/write operations. Small LLM inference tasks on 135M parameter models yield average generation rates, whereas medium 7B parameter model workloads demonstrate poor execution speed due to memory bandwidth limits.

From a resource density and cost efficiency perspective, the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation offers a standard baseline configuration without requiring financial commitments to local NVMe storage. While constrained in high-concurrency database operations and heavy memory-bound throughput, the c3d-standard-4 provides reliable dedicated compute for light single-threaded processing, minor web serving, basic text processing, and general-purpose entry-level workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor (2 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and 16 GB of RAM. Featuring x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 instruction support, the instance delivers strong single-core CPU benchmark performance in the top 25% range. However, multi-core scaling and uncached memory bandwidth show notable performance trade-offs, placing in the bottom 25% across multi-threaded synthetic tests. The system contains no local disk storage or GPU hardware. Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, c3d-standard-4 offers cost-effective execution for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic general-purpose compute workloads that do not demand high memory throughput or heavy concurrent execution.
